{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-01",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Public sign-in page", "Magic-link email sender", "Link verification endpoint", "Customer billing portal", "Card-on-file update"],
    "dataStores": ["Customer accounts", "Invoices", "Stored card references"],
    "externalServices": ["Email delivery provider"],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Internet to public sign-in page", "Email inbox to portal session", "Portal to payment card store"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii", "payment"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Sign-in link stays usable for 7 days, so a leaked link is a 7-day account takeover",
      "scenario": "The design says the link \"stays valid for 7 days\" and is not described as single-use. Anyone who sees the email later (shared or family inbox, forwarded invoice thread, a device left signed into webmail, a mailbox breached days earlier) can replay the same link and land signed in as that customer, read invoices and change the card on file. No password or second factor stands in the way.",
      "component": "Link verification endpoint",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "one", "harm": "takeover" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "we email them a sign-in link. The link opens the portal already signed in and stays valid for 7 days." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-613"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could reuse a stolen sign-in link for a whole week and get straight into a customer's billing account.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Magic links are single-use and short-lived",
        "given": "a customer has requested a sign-in link",
        "when": "the link is used a second time, or more than 15 minutes after it was issued",
        "then": "the portal rejects it, asks for a fresh link, and invalidates any earlier unused links for that email"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Guessable sign-in tokens let an attacker sign in as any customer",
      "scenario": "The design states only that a link is emailed and \"opens the portal already signed in\"; nothing specifies that the token is long and generated with a cryptographic random source. If the token is short, sequential, or derived from the email or a timestamp, an attacker can generate or brute-force valid links against the public endpoint and sign in as arbitrary customers, reading invoices and changing cards for many accounts.",
      "component": "Magic-link token generation",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "medium", "reach": "all", "harm": "takeover" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "we email them a sign-in link. The link opens the portal already signed in" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-330", "CWE-307"],
      "plainLanguage": "If the sign-in links are predictable, an attacker can make up links and walk into other people's accounts.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Sign-in tokens are unpredictable and brute-force resistant",
        "given": "the portal issues magic-link sign-in tokens",
        "when": "a token is created or a token value is submitted",
        "then": "the token carries at least 128 bits of cryptographically random entropy, is stored hashed, and repeated invalid token submissions from an IP or against an account are throttled and alerted"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Card on file can be changed with nothing more than a sign-in link",
      "scenario": "The portal \"lets customers change the card on file\" and the only credential is the emailed link. An attacker holding a leaked or replayed link swaps the stored card for one they control, or points future refunds and credits at their own card, with no step-up verification and no notification described. Because the design is for a billing portal, this directly moves money.",
      "component": "Card-on-file update",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "one", "harm": "money" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The portal shows invoices and lets customers change the card on file." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-620"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone who gets hold of a sign-in link could replace the saved payment card without proving who they are.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Changing payment details needs step-up verification",
        "given": "a session that was created from a magic link",
        "when": "the customer tries to change the card on file",
        "then": "the portal requires a fresh verification (a new code sent to the registered email or a second factor) within the last few minutes and emails the customer a change notification"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Public sign-in page reveals which email addresses have accounts",
      "scenario": "The sign-in page is public and takes only an email address. If it answers differently for a known customer (\"check your inbox\") than for an unknown one, or differs in timing, anyone can test lists of email addresses and learn who is a customer. Combined with billing context that is commercially sensitive personal data and fuels targeted phishing that asks for a sign-in link.",
      "component": "Public sign-in page",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 2,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "personal_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers sign in to the billing portal by entering their email address" },
        { "quote": "The sign-in page is public." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-204"],
      "plainLanguage": "An outsider could type in email addresses one by one and find out which ones are customers.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Sign-in response does not disclose account existence",
        "given": "an unauthenticated visitor on the public sign-in page",
        "when": "they submit any email address, registered or not",
        "then": "the page returns the same message, status code and comparable response time, and no email is sent for unknown addresses"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Anyone can drive unlimited sign-in emails to any customer address",
      "scenario": "The sign-in form is public and unauthenticated, and submitting an email triggers an outbound message. A bot can submit one victim's address thousands of times to bury their inbox (hiding a real fraud alert), or submit large harvested lists to run up email costs and get the sending domain blocklisted, which then breaks sign-in for every real customer.",
      "component": "Magic-link email sender",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "availability" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Customers sign in to the billing portal by entering their email address; we email them a sign-in link." },
        { "quote": "The sign-in page is public." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770"],
      "plainLanguage": "A bot could spam the sign-in form so customers get flooded with emails and our mail domain gets blocked.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Sign-in link requests are rate limited and bot resistant",
        "given": "the public sign-in form",
        "when": "requests arrive repeatedly for the same email address or from the same source",
        "then": "the service caps links per address per hour and per day, applies a global send budget with alerting, and requires a bot challenge once thresholds are crossed"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Sign-in token in the URL leaks through history, logs and referrers",
      "scenario": "The credential is the link itself, so the token travels in the URL. It is then kept in browser history and shared-computer autocomplete, written to proxy, CDN and web server access logs, and can be passed to third parties in the Referer header or in analytics from the landing page. Anyone with log access or the shared browser can lift a still-valid token and sign in as the customer.",
      "component": "Link verification endpoint",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "takeover" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The link opens the portal already signed in and stays valid for 7 days." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-598"],
      "plainLanguage": "Because the login secret is part of the web address, it can end up in logs or browser history where others can find it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Token is consumed immediately and never retained in URLs or logs",
        "given": "a customer opens a magic link",
        "when": "the verification endpoint handles the request",
        "then": "it exchanges the token for a session cookie, redirects to a URL with no token, marks the token used, scrubs the token from access logs, and sets a referrer policy that stops it leaking to third parties"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Invoices and card details stay reachable from stale sessions with no sign-out or binding",
      "scenario": "A link that already signs the user in for seven days, with no described session lifetime, device binding or sign-out, means a session created on a shared or kiosk browser stays privileged long after the customer walks away. The next person at that machine opens the portal and sees invoices with names, addresses and amounts, plus the stored card, and can change it.",
      "component": "Customer billing portal session",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "anyone", "effort": "low", "reach": "one", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "The link opens the portal already signed in and stays valid for 7 days. The portal shows invoices and lets customers change the card on file." }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-613"],
      "plainLanguage": "A session left open on a shared computer could let the next person read invoices and change the saved card.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Portal sessions expire and can be revoked",
        "given": "a signed-in portal session",
        "when": "it is idle for 15 minutes, reaches an absolute lifetime of 12 hours, or the customer uses sign out",
        "then": "the session is invalidated server side, a visible sign-out control exists on every page, and the customer can revoke all other active sessions"
      }
    }
  ]
}
